title: AI Content Checklist Before You Publish | AIVideosUGC
description: A pre-publish AI content checklist for product photos and video ads: match product details, add prices yourself, and follow platform rules. Save it now.
h1: An AI Content Checklist for Product Photos and Video Ads
lead: An AI content checklist is a last look at the product, the words, and the rights before a photo or a video goes on your store, a marketplace, or an ad account.
summary: Match the product, add prices yourself, license what appears, and follow the current labeling rule for each site you post on.

paras: What to review, how to check a still, how to check a clip, where the price goes, what you need the rights to use, and when to label a generated person.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain black travel backpack beside a blank laptop and a blank phone.

sections.h2: What belongs on an AI content checklist?
paras: Check the product against what you ship, then the words, then the rights, then the rule for the site where it will appear.

A generated photo or video is a new picture built from your upload, not a copy of the original file. A logo letter can shift, a button can move, a piece can appear, or a color can drift. The same pass works for a listing photo, a social post, and a paid ad.
sections.alt: Hands check the front pocket and zipper of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: How do I check AI product images?
paras: Hold the real item, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through color, shape, logos, parts, and size.

Compare color in daylight, not only on a bright monitor. Count pockets, straps, and buckles. Read every letter on a label. If a hand or a familiar object is in the frame, the product should look the right size beside it. A styled scene might add a candle or a plant. That is fine as decoration only if a shopper would not think it comes in the order. [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos) are where those scenes are made, so review them with the same part count.
sections.alt: Hands count pockets, buckles and straps on plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: What is on an AI video review checklist?
paras: Play the clip full screen on your phone, then step through it slowly, with extra attention on the hands and the first frame.

Movement is where a clip tends to slip: a label can blur as the product turns, fingers can blend into a strap, or a zipper can change shape halfway through. Count fingers and watch how they grip. The first frame often becomes the thumbnail. If one short moment is off, trim around it in your editor. If the problem runs through the clip, make a new version. Run this same check on an [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) clip before you post it.
sections.alt: Hands open the zipper and flap of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: Which checks should I do before I publish the price?
paras: Make the picture first, then add the price, the date, the code, and the headline yourself.

Do not ask for those words inside the image or the clip. Generated lettering is often garbled. Add them in Canva, CapCut, or Ads Manager, where you control every character. Before posting, match the price and the code to the store, and confirm any end date has not already passed. If stray letters appear on packaging or on a sign in the background, crop them out or try again.
sections.alt: Plain black travel backpack centered on a white background.

sections.h2: What do I need to own before an AI ad goes live?
paras: Upload only photos you took or have the rights to use, and feature only logos that belong to you.

If you start from a supplier photo, your agreement with them needs to cover ads. Requests built around another company's marks, or around celebrities, may be refused. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded. For music, pick a track from the commercial library in your editor or ad account, or a track you have licensed for advertising.
sections.alt: Hands hold plain black travel backpack beside a plain camera and blank phone.

sections.h2: When do AI-generated content labels apply?
paras: Read the current rule on each site you post to. Several platforms ask you to mark realistic generated people or scenes, and the rule changes.

Keep two rules on every site. Do not present a generated person as a real customer or reviewer, including in [AI model photos for clothing](page:model-photos). And do not let a caption promise health, skin, or weight results. Show how the product is used and let the shopper decide.
The product must match the box, the words must be yours, and the photo, logo, and music must be yours or licensed.
Then follow the current labeling rule for the site you are posting on. If a buyer could feel misled, do not publish that file.

faq.q: What should I check before posting an AI-made video?
faq.a: Watch it on your phone from the first frame to the last. Confirm the product, the hands, and the label, then confirm any price you added matches the store.

faq.q: What if a prop looks like it comes with the order?
faq.a: Do not use that version, or say clearly in the listing what is included. Decoration is fine only when a shopper would not expect it in the box.

faq.q: Can I ask the tool to draw my discount code?
faq.a: No. Add the code, the price, and the date yourself after download so the characters stay correct.

faq.q: Do I have to say a person is generated?
faq.a: Check the current rule for each platform or marketplace you use. Do not describe a generated person as a real customer, even where the site lets you mark the ad as generated.

faq.q: Can I use a supplier photo as the source?
faq.a: Only if your agreement with the supplier covers ads. Otherwise shoot your own photo.

faq.q: What if one moment in the clip looks wrong?
faq.a: Trim that moment in your editor if it is brief. If the error runs through the clip, make a new version instead of posting it.

cta_title: Check every product detail before your next ad
cta_lead: Upload a product photo, compare the result with the item you ship, and add your own price before it goes live.
